study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Tabbal et al., npj Parkinson's Disease, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study aggregated EEG data from 14 distinct sites/studies (Dataset 1 through 14). None of the 14 datasets correspond to named datasets in the provided Minor Category list. The 14 sites are: (1) AHEPA University Hospital, Thessaloniki, Greece; (2) Technical University of Munich, Germany; (3) BASEL - University Hospital of Basel, Switzerland; (4) University of New Mexico, USA; (5) CREAPARK - University Hospital of Rennes, France; (6) turkeyAD - Izmir, Turkey; (7) turkeyPDAD - Istanbul, Turkey; (8) lebAD2017 - Al-Ajaza and Mazloum Hospital, Lebanon; (9) lebAD2019 - VitaNova PolyClinic, Lebanon; (10) UMHC - University of Marseille, France; (11) University Hospital of Turku, Finland; (12) WCHC - Wadsworth Center, New York, USA; (13) SRM - University of Oslo, Norway; (14) DIH - Denmark. Since N>=2 sites are used and no dataset matches a named category, this is classified as MULTI-SITE (N>=2).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The data were aggregated from 14 distinct studies, each approved by its local ethics committee"; "Resting-state eyes-closed EEG data was collected from subjects aged 40 to 92 years, across 14 sites"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Methods / Datasets, L169; Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Results / Data description, L39

answer.MULTI-SITE (N>=2): HC from all 14 sites used for normative model training (80%, n=400) and held-out testing (20%, n=99); PD patients (n=237) and AD patients (n=197) used for clinical transfer/deviation analysis

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls from 14 multi-site EEG datasets were split 80/20 for normative model training and testing. Clinical groups (PD, AD) were projected onto the trained models to derive individual deviation scores for heterogeneity characterization and clinical correlation analyses.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out as a comparison group against the clinical cohort. The clinical groups comprised 237 PD patients (65% M), and 197 AD patients (37% M)."; "we trained GAMLSS models for each channel/connection across all frequency bands using the healthy control training group HC(train) (80% of the healthy sample). Subsequently, we projected the features data ... of our clinical groups (PD, and AD) and the held-out healthy control testing group HC(test) (remaining 20% of the healthy sample), onto the corresponding models."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Results / Data description, L39; Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Methods / Deviation and overlap maps, L215

model-1.model-name: GAMLSS normative model (EEG spectral power and functional connectivity)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative modeling framework (GAMLSS) was applied to two types of EEG features: scalp-level relative spectral power (19 channels x 5 frequency bands) and source-level functional connectivity (68 ROIs, pairwise AEC x 5 frequency bands). Both feature types used the same HC cohort split. Total HC = 499, of which 400 (80%) were used for training and 99 (20%) held out for testing.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Our cohort consisted of 933 individuals, subdivided into a group of healthy controls (N=400 in the training set, N=99 in the held-out testing set)"; "Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out as a comparison group against the clinical cohort."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Methods / Datasets, L168-L169; Tabbal2025.pdf.md: Results / Data description, L39

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The supplementary table (Supplementary Data 1) reports per-dataset median ages and SDs for HC, but not means. Weighted mean was computed using medians as proxies: sum(n_i * median_i) / 499 = 30724/499 = 61.57. Pooled SD = sqrt(sum((n_i - 1) * sd_i^2) / (499 - 14)) = sqrt(31329/485) = 8.04. Min/max are the extremes of all per-dataset age ranges (40 from Datasets 2, 10, 12, 13; 87 from Dataset 6). The paper reports overall cohort (all 933 subjects) mean = 64.95 +/- 10.28, but this includes patients. Train-phase age breakdown is not reported separately.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "All participants were aged above 40 years old (mean = 64.95 +/- 10.28; 48% M)"; Supplementary Data 1 per-dataset HC demographics: Dataset 1: n=29, median=67, SD=5, [57-78]; Dataset 2: n=22, median=66, SD=10, [40-79]; Dataset 3: n=31, median=66, SD=6, [53-75]; Dataset 4: n=24, median=69, SD=10, [48-84]; Dataset 5: n=21, median=58, SD=8, [46-68]; Dataset 6: n=93, median=67, SD=8, [44-87]; Dataset 7: n=63, median=63, SD=7, [51-79]; Dataset 8: n=10, median=70, SD=5, [64-81]; Dataset 9: n=13, median=60, SD=6, [55-71]; Dataset 10: n=64, median=54, SD=11, [40-75]; Dataset 11: n=20, median=78, SD=6, [53-76]; Dataset 12: n=44, median=49, SD=6, [40-67]; Dataset 13: n=43, median=51, SD=9, [40-71]; Dataset 14: n=22, median=62, SD=7, [53-76]

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Overall HC sex counts derived from the paper's train/test sex ratios: HC(train) = 400 with 46% M = 184 males, 216 females; HC(test) = 99 with 42% M = 42 males (rounded from 41.58), 57 females. Overall: 184 + 42 = 226 males (45.3%), 216 + 57 = 273 females (54.7%), totalling 499.
